`UsbIo` needs a microcontroller with **native USB** it can add a vendor
control endpoint to. Every board below has been checked against ArduinoDriver's
own board-support table; "compile-verified" means the example sketch builds
warning-free for that board, not that it has been run on real hardware — only
the Portenta H7 has.

## Compile-verified boards

@tbl-boards-detail gives the FQBN, pin layout and resolutions for every board
ArduinoDriver currently supports.

| Board | FQBN | Pins | Analog in (AIN) | DAC | PWM | ADC / PWM / DAC bits | Logic | Streaming | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Portenta H7 (M7 core) | `arduino:mbed_portenta:envie_m7` | 26 (D0–D14, A0–A6, D22, LEDs 23–25) | A0–A6 = pins 15–21 (A0–A3 analog-only pads) | pin 21 (A6) | every core-PWM-capable pin | 16 / 12 / 12 | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| GIGA R1 WiFi | `arduino:mbed_giga:giga` | 103 (D0–D102) | A0–A7, A12, A13 = pins 76–85 | pins 84, 85 | core-PWM-capable pins | 16 / 12 / 12 | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| Nano 33 BLE | `arduino:mbed_nano:nano33ble` | 26 | pins 14–21 | none | every pin | 16 (12 significant) / 12 / – | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| Nano RP2040 Connect | `arduino:mbed_nano:nanorp2040connect` | 30 | pins 14–17 (GPIO26–29) | none | every pin | 16 (12 significant) / 12 / – | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| UNO R4 Minima | `arduino:renesas_uno:minima` | 20 | pins 14–19 | pin 14 (A0) | 0–13, 18, 19 | 14 / 12 / 12 | 5 V | no | no |
| Nano R4 | `arduino:renesas_uno:nanor4` | 26 | pins 14–21 | pin 14 | 0–13, 18, 19 | 14 / 12 / 12 | 5 V | no | no |
| Zero | `arduino:samd:arduino_zero_native` | 20 | pins 14–19 | pin 14 | 3–13, 15, 16 | 12 / 10 / 10 | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| MKR Zero (MKR family) | `arduino:samd:mkrzero` | 33 (LED = 32) | pins 15–21 (A0=15) | pin 15 (A0) | 0–8, 10, 18, 19 | 12 / 10 / 10 | 3.3 V | yes | yes |
| Nano 33 IoT | `arduino:samd:nano_33_iot` | 31 | pins 14–21 | pin 14 | 2–6, 9–12, 16, 17, 19, 29, 30 | 12 / 10 / 10 | 3.3 V | yes | yes |

: Per-board pin layout and resolutions, from the README's "Board support"
table. {#tbl-boards-detail}

A few boards have pins that are not on the header but are still addressable,
because the core itself counts them as digital pins: the GIGA R1 WiFi's
D89–D102 (SPI header, USB-host enable, Wi-Fi/BLE control, BOOT0, SCL1/SDA1)
and the Nano RP2040 Connect's D24–D29 (the NINA module's reset/SPI/UART
lines). A `RESET` (from `arduino-io reset` or the library) puts *all* of
these back to `INPUT`, exactly as it does for header pins.

::: {.callout-note}
## Analog pin numbers are board-specific

Pin numbers are the same numbers you would pass to `digitalRead()` or
`analogRead()` in a sketch, and the analog pins do not have fixed numbers
across boards: **A0 is pin 15 on a Portenta H7 and pin 14 on an UNO R4**.
Always check the board you actually have, not another table.

```bash
arduino-io caps
```

lists every pin and what it can do:

```
PIN  CAPS  NOTES
0    D-P-
...
15   -A--  analog #0 (analog-only pad)
...
21   DA-C  analog #6, DAC
D digital I/O, A analog input, P PWM, C DAC
```
:::

## Not supported

- **UNO R3, Mega 2560, classic Nano** — not possible. Their USB port is a
  separate chip (16U2 or CH340); the microcontroller that owns the pins has
  no USB of its own for `UsbIo` to attach to.
- **UNO R4 WiFi** — not supported. Its USB-C port belongs to the board's
  ESP32-S3 co-processor, not the RA4M1 that runs the sketch; the RA4M1's own
  USB is disabled (`-DNO_USB`) on this board.

## Experimental and unverified

- **RP2040/RP2350 boards** via the `arduino-pico` core (`rp2040:rp2040:*`) —
  a transport shim is written but the core is not installed in
  ArduinoDriver's own build, so it is untested.
- **ESP32-S2/S3** via `arduino-esp32` (`esp32:esp32:*`) — a transport shim is
  written; it needs *USB Mode: USB-OTG (TinyUSB)* and is likewise untested.
- **Teensy 4.x, STM32duino** — deferred. Neither core exposes a
  vendor-request hook the way mbed, SAMD and Renesas do; supporting them
  would need a patched core.

Do not build a bench around any of these three categories.

## Which board for which experiment

@tbl-board-experiments gives the rule the [recommendation
matrix](index.qmd#board-recommendation) already applies.

| Experiments | Requirement | Suitable boards |
|---|---|---|
| S2, M3 | streaming **and** a high loop rate | Portenta H7 is verified; other streaming-capable boards need their own rate check first (see the [stream verification](verify.qmd)) |
| S1, S3 | streaming | any board with `streaming` in `arduino-io info`'s `flags` line — every board in @tbl-boards-detail except UNO R4 Minima and Nano R4 |
| T1–T3, M1, M2 | any supported board | every board in @tbl-boards-detail |

: Board requirements by AMLab experiment group. {#tbl-board-experiments}

S2 (dynamic DAQ characterization) and M3 (vibration) push the sampling rate,
so they need both a streaming-capable board *and* a loop fast enough to hit
the target rate — currently only measured on the Portenta H7. S1 (static DAQ
characterization) and S3 (aliasing and filtering) need streaming but not an
extreme rate. Everything in the thermal strand and M1/M2 samples slowly
enough that any supported board, streaming or not, works — including the two
Renesas boards.
